page.layout: One column of running text, set in a single block. Running head at the top above the text, page number at the top right. Signature at the foot left of centre. No marginal notes in the text margins. A handwritten or stamped "646" sits in the right margin and is not printed text.

main_text.p: Numerus, Casus, Declinatio, Persona, Species & similia accidentia sunt adsignificantia, & dicuntur adsignificatio-nes respectu significantium & significationum: Amo, Ma-gister, Ego, quorū hæc attributa sunt πτωτικά[?]. 3[?], De idem significandis: idem declaratio [illegible, ~8 letters], quæ interdum dicuntur συνωνύμια[?], Synonyma: interdum παρωνύμια[?], polyonyma, quia una res duo habet vel plura nomina: 1[?] alia sunt ubique esse & omnipræsens esse. Ex Arist. & Damasc. hoc alibi ostendi.
main_text.head: An signo attribuatur nonnunquam res significata?
main_text.p: Signum sæpe nomen rei significatæ accipit: ut, panis Eucharisticus nomen corporis Domini. Augustin. ad Bonifacium Epist. 23. Si Sacramenta quandam similitudinem earum rerum, quarum sunt sacramenta, non haberent, omnino sacramenta non essent. Ex similitudine autem hac plerumque etiam ipsarum rerum nomina accipiunt. Sacramentum corporis est corpus Christi, secundum quendam modum, &c. & paulo post: Consepulti, inquit Apostolus, sumus Christo per Baptismum in mortem. Non ait, sepulturam significamus, sed prorsus ait, consepulti sumus. Sacramentum ergo tantæ rei, nonnisi eiusdem rei vocabulo nuncupatur. Idem lib. 4. de doctrina Christiana, cap. 20. Petra erat Christus, quia petra illa typum habuit corporis Christi. De Trinitate lib. 3. cap. 4. Illud corpus & sanguinem Christi dicimus, quod ex frugibus terræ acceptum & precé mystica consecratum rite sumimus; ad salutem spiritualem, in memoriam pro nobis Dominicæ passionis. Cyprianus de unctione Chrismatis. In mensa Domini significantia, & significata iisdem vocabulis censentur. Panis igitur Eucharisticus est ipsum corpus Christi, mystice, id est, per modum mysterii significantis aliud, quam videtur, & non ipsum essentialiter. At enim, inquit noster adversarius, sicut res significata prædicatur Corpus Dominicum de sacramentali pane, non prædicabitur, ut effectum de instrumento seu medio externo. Respondeo ego, puerilis hæc esse nugas, hanc consecutionem nullam esse, cum panis Eucharistias & signi ac testimonii, & externi medii instrumentique rationem habeat. page.notes: Page number "81" is read from a faint mark at top right and is uncertain. The "646" in the right margin is a later annotation or stamp, not printed text, and is left out. The Greek words after "quorū hæc attributa sunt" and in the Synonyma/Polyonyma line are doubtful and marked [?]; the words after "idem declaratio" could not be read and are marked illegible. The "3" and "1" in the first paragraph are uncertain. The signature "Fff" is read from the foot. The text ends mid-word with "lo-", continued on the next page. No catchword is visible. The faint marks at the lower left and right corners are not transcribed. "Augustin." is read from "Auguft n." with the long s written as plain s. "Eucharistias" is kept as printed. The word "significantia" in "significantia, & significata" is printed as "significant a", read here as a likely line-break split of "significantia" and marked accordingly in the reading, with the printed hyphenation not visible.
